source_title: India aim to seal New Zealand T20I series as Bhuvneshwar, Sooryavanshi eye redemption - India Today
source_excerpt:
NZ vs IND, 3rd T20I: India will look to seal the T20I series against New Zealand in Wellington, with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi seeking redemption and Bhuvneshwar Kumar aiming to rediscover his bowling form. New Zealand, meanwhile, will rely on their in-form batters and a depleted pace attack as they attempt to keep the series alive.
India are one win away from sealing the T20I series against New Zealand, but the third match in Wellington on Tuesday, October 27, offers more than just an opportunity to take an unassailable 3-0 lead. Led by Shreyas Iyer, India will look to maintain their winning momentum while addressing a few concerns that have emerged despite their impressive start.
Bhuvneshwar Kumar will be keen to rediscover his rhythm with the ball, while teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will look to make a stronger impression after a disappointing outing in Christchurch.
India have won the first two matches by four wickets each, chasing down targets of 226 and 181. Their batting depth has repeatedly come to the rescue, but the bowling unit has struggled to contain New Zealand's aggressive approach.
The hosts, meanwhile, have their own concerns, with Matt Henry ruled out of the remainder of the series and Lockie Ferguson unavailable for the Wellington clash.
Ishan Kishan's absence has opened the door for Sooryavanshi to make his mark. Kishan has been ruled out of the third T20I after sustaining a low-grade right adductor strain during the series opener. His availability for the remaining matches remains uncertain as he continues his recovery.
Sooryavanshi, who managed just four runs off eight deliveries in the second T20I, will be eager to put that outing behind him. The 15-year-old has had limited opportunities since his debut in July, and a substantial contribution in Wellington would strengthen his case for a longer run in the side. It could also give the selectors a welcome dilemma when Kishan returns to contention.
If Kishan remains unavailable, Sooryavanshi could get further opportunities in the remaining matches, allowing him to gain valuable experience and demonstrate that he can handle the demands of the role.
India's other batters have already offered encouraging signs. Sanju Samson made a blistering 67 in the series opener, although he fell cheaply in the second match. Abhishek Sharma has provided brisk starts in both games, scoring 29 and 27 respectively.
Shreyas Iyer contributed 42 in the opener, while Tilak Varma came to India's rescue in Christchurch with an unbeaten 51 off 26 balls after the visitors slipped to 70 for five. Naman Dhir has also impressed, smashing 42 off 15 balls in the first match before adding 31 in the second. Nitish Kumar Reddy's unbeaten 26 further underlined India's batting depth.
The challenge now is to turn these individual contributions into a more complete team performance, particularly with the ball. CAN BHUVNESHWAR FIGHT BACK? Bhuvneshwar Kumar has leaked 99 runs in the first two T20Is. Courtesy: AFP
For Bhuvneshwar, the third T20I presents an opportunity to hit the reset button. The experienced pacer has conceded 99 runs in eight overs across the first two matches at an economy rate of 12.37, taking just one wicket. Those figures fall well short of the standards he has set throughout his career.
The 36-year-old returned to India's T20I setup after nearly four years, having enjoyed an impressive IPL 2026 campaign in which he claimed 28 wickets for Royal Challengers Bengaluru. However, his comeback has not gone to plan, with New Zealand's batters repeatedly finding ways to put him under pressure.
Bhuvneshwar built his reputation on swing, control and the ability to outthink batters, particularly at the death. Those qualities made him one of India's most dependable white-ball bowlers, and he will be eager to rediscover them in Wellington.
The task will not be easy against a New Zealand side that has shown little hesitation in taking the attack to India's bowlers. Bhuvneshwar will need to make the most of any movement on offer, tighten his lines and avoid the loose deliveries that have proved costly. A disciplined spell could help restore his confidence and strengthen his case for the remaining matches. advertisement NEW ZEALAND'S BATTING FIRES, BUT PACE ATTACK TAKES A HIT Matt Henry won't be a part of the last 3 T20Is. Courtesy: AFP New Zealand's batting has been a bright spot despite trailing in the series. Glenn Phillips led the charge in the opening T20I with an explosive unbeaten 82 off 40 balls, while Finn Allen and Bevon Jacobs also made valuable contributions. The hosts continued to score at a healthy rate in the second match, but their bowlers struggled to defend the target as India completed another successful chase. Their task has been complicated by injuries and workload concerns in the pace department. Henry has been ruled out of the remainder of the series , while Ferguson will miss the Wellington clash and is expected to return for the final two matches. advertisement New Zealand have turned to their squad depth to cover the gaps. Matt Fisher has travelled as cover for the third T20I, Blair Tickner is set to join for the final three matches, and Josh Clarkson will be available for the last two. Kyle Jamieson is an option in Wellington before returning to domestic duties with Canterbury. With their pace resources stretched, New Zealand need their available bowlers to disrupt India's deep batting line-up. Captain Mitchell Santner provided a boost in Christchurch with a four-wicket haul, but the rest of the attack must offer greater support. Tighter lines and better execution in crucial phases will be vital if the hosts are to prevent India from sealing the series. WELLINGTON PITCH AND WEATHER CONDITIONS The pitch in Wellington has been a sporting one with the average score around 165 from the 18 T20Is that has been played at the venue since 2016. Teams chasing have won 10 matches and hence, batting second should be the way forward for teams. Wellington is expected to be windy with swirling gusts of up to 55 km/h reported on the eve of the match. Although the winds are forecast to ease slightly on Tuesday, they could still influence shot-making, high catches and bowling plans.
